chapters.title: From the Stone Age to Ashoka (to 232 BCE)
chapters.intro:
From the first stone tools to the death of Ashoka. Learn how people moved from hunting to farming, built the planned Harappan cities, composed the Vedas, formed the sixteen mahajanapadas, heard the Buddha and Mahavira, and how Magadha grew into the Mauryan empire (NCERT). Andhra appears early: Kurnool's Stone Age caves, the ash mounds, megaliths, the Assaka mahajanapada and Ashoka's edicts at Erragudi and Amaravati.

BCE years count down: 600 BCE is earlier than 500 BCE. Most early dates are approximate (c.).

fragments.title: The Stone Age
fragments.intro: Palaeolithic hand-axes, Mesolithic microliths, the first farmers at Mehrgarh, and the Kurnool caves.

fragments.title: The Harappan civilisation
fragments.intro: NCERT's 6000–1300 BCE: early villages, the great cities, trade with Mesopotamia, and the decline.

fragments.title: Vedas, mahajanapadas, Buddha and Mahavira
fragments.intro: The Rigveda and later Vedas, iron and megaliths, the sixteen mahajanapadas, the Persians, Mahavira and the Buddha, Magadha and the Nandas.

fragments.title: The Mauryan empire
fragments.intro: Alexander and Porus, Chandragupta and Chanakya, Seleucus and Megasthenes, Ashoka, Kalinga and dhamma.

takeaways: First Indian hand-axe: Pallavaram (R.B. Foote, 1863); Mehrgarh c. 7000 BCE is the earliest farming site.
Harappan civilisation 6000–1300 BCE; mature cities 2600–1900 BCE; announced by John Marshall in 1924 (NCERT).
Rigveda c. 1500–1000 BCE; Later Vedic 1000–500 BCE (NCERT).
Sixteen mahajanapadas c. 600 BCE; Assaka the only one in the south (NCERT).
Mahavira 24th tirthankara; Buddha: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kusinagara (NCERT).
Alexander 327–325 BCE; Chandragupta Maurya c. 321 BCE; Ashoka c. 268–231 BCE; Kalinga c. 261 BCE (NCERT).
chapters.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 1 "Bricks, Beads and Bones"; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 4 "Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings"

pegs.hook: About 2600 BCE: the Harappan cities. "Harappa is 4,600 years old" — 2600 BCE plus 2000 CE.
About 563 BCE: the Buddha is born; Mahavira about the same age. Think "6th century BCE: two teachers, sixteen mahajanapadas".
326 BCE: Alexander at the Hydaspes. Chandragupta rises five years later (321 BCE).
261 BCE: Kalinga war; Ashoka turns to dhamma. He dies 232 BCE — the end of this chapter.

chapters.title: From the Satavahanas to Harsha (231 BCE – 647 CE)
chapters.intro:
After the Mauryas, India split into many kingdoms: Shungas, Indo-Greeks, Shakas and Kushanas in the north; Satavahanas and Ikshvakus in the Deccan and Andhra; Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas in the Tamil land (NCERT). Then the Guptas united the north (c. 320 CE) and Harsha ruled from Kanauj (606–647 CE), while the Chalukyas and Pallavas fought in the south.

Andhra is at the centre of this story: Bhattiprolu, Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda, the Vishnukundins and the start of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

fragments.title: After the Mauryas
fragments.intro: Satavahanas, Shungas, Indo-Greeks, Kharavela, the Vikram and Saka eras, Kanishka and Karikala.

fragments.title: Satavahanas, Shakas and Ikshvakus
fragments.intro: Ashvaghosha, Gautamiputra Satakarni, Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription, Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda and the end of the Sangam age.

fragments.title: The Guptas
fragments.intro: Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, Fa-Hien, Nalanda, Ajanta, Aryabhata, the Hunas and the Vishnukundins.

fragments.title: Harsha, Chalukyas and Pallavas
fragments.intro: Badami Chalukyas, Aihole, Harsha of Kanauj, Xuanzang, Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi, Pulakeshin II and the sack of Vatapi.

takeaways: Mauryas end c. 185 BCE; Shungas, Indo-Greeks (c. 200–100 BCE), Satavahanas in the Deccan (NCERT).
Saka era 78 CE (Kanishka); Vikram Samvat 57 BCE.
Gautamiputra Satakarni: Nasik inscription; Rudradaman: Junagadh inscription, Sudarshana lake (NCERT).
Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) and Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri, Ikshvakus) in Andhra.
Guptas from c. 320 CE; Prayaga prashasti by Harisena; Chandragupta II c. 375–415 CE (NCERT).
Harsha 606–647 CE; Xuanzang; Aihole inscription 634 CE by Ravikirti (NCERT); Eastern Chalukyas 624 CE.
chapters.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 4 "Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings"; Andhra Pradesh history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

pegs.hook: 78 CE: the Shaka era begins (Kanishka by tradition) — India's national calendar (adopted 1957).
320 CE: the Gupta era begins with Chandragupta I. "320 = three-two-zero, the golden age starts".
606 CE: Harsha's era; he dies 647 — the end of ancient India in most books.
